statement: The second stages for spectra and mod-$p$ coefficients — Fix a Grothendieck universe $\mathcal U$, and use a larger universe for categories of $\mathcal U$-small objects. Let $\mathcal C$ be either $\operatorname{Sp}_{\mathcal U}$ or $D(\mathbb F_p)$, with its indicated presentable infinity-category enhancement. We number the stages by \[ W_{\mathcal C}^{(0)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C}},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C}}^{\mathrm{lc}}, \qquad \mathcal C_1=\mathcal S_{W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)}=W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C_1}}^{\mathrm{lc}}. \tag{I.9.1} \] Here $\mathcal S_W$ is the accessible reflective localization of spaces at exactly the class $W$, and $\mathbb D_{\mathcal E}(A)=\operatorname{Ho}\operatorname{Fun}(NA^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E)$. The localizations in (I.9.1) exist and preserve finite products. Their constant-coefficient classes satisfy $W_{\mathbb D_{\mathcal C_1}}=W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)}$. For every map $u:X\to Y$ of small spaces, \[ u\in W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi_0(u)\text{ is bijective and } \Omega_xu\in W_{\mathcal C}^{(1)} \text{ for one basepoint in every component of }X. \tag{I.9.2} \] Consequently \[ W_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{(1)} =W_{\operatorname{Sp}}^{(2)}=W_\infty, \tag{I.9.3} \] and \[ u\in W_{D(\mathbb F_p)}^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \pi_0(u)\text{ is bijective},\\ \pi_1(u),\pi_2(u)\text{ are integral isomorphisms at every basepoint},\\ H_*(X\langle2\rangle;\mathbb F_p)\longrightarrow H_*(Y\langle2\rangle;\mathbb F_p) \text{ is an isomorphism on each corresponding component}. \end{cases} \tag{I.9.4} \] For a pointed connected component, $X\langle2\rangle$ means the homotopy fibre at its chosen basepoint of $X\to\tau_{\leq2}X$. The displayed map of covers is the one induced by $u$ and the basepoints. There are no nilpotence or finite-type hypotheses. The second class is again accessible and product stable, so $\mathcal C_2=\mathcal S_{W_{\mathcal C}^{(2)}}$ realizes it as an ordinary constant-coefficient class. This construction can be iterated at every finite stage for these two starting coefficients. It is a specified realization by localized spaces; functorial construction on all bare derivators and all exact morphisms remains the separate Open assertion of I.7.
depends_on: D.5; Lurie HA Theorem4.7.3.5; Lurie HTT Proposition5.5.4.15; Rivera2022 Theorem1; Rivera–Wierstra–Zeinalian2022 Proposition4
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Prompt I(3), concrete enhanced second stages for spectra and D(F_p); GALOIS E.8/E.10 independently checked; bare-derivator GALOIS E.11/G.6 remains Open
notes: Stage0 is the ordinary constant class; stage1 is the locally constant class of the original coefficient; stage2 is the locally constant class of its exact localized-space realization. Spectra give W_infinity at stages1 and2. F_p gives component bijections, integral pi1/pi2 isomorphisms and F_p-homology equivalences of the specified 2-connected covers. Accessibility is proved by a bounded finite-support construction, without a large-cardinal assumption. This does not construct functoriality on all bare derivators or all exact morphisms.
